description.value:
Frequency once per day

Targets 1 creature, body or fading spirit that does not meet a Passing's ordinary requirements

You perform a Passing on something the rite was not built to reach — a body with nobody left in it, a spirit already halfway gone, a soul with no name you know. Ignore the requirement that the target be an incapacitated or willing spirit or undead creature. The Passing costs two thresholds more than it otherwise would, and you pay that cost whether or not there was anything there to ferry.

cinderfall.incomplete: Ashcantor's entire signature resource system (Passage, a Passing, Walking Through, Embers, Ash-Light) has zero rule-element representation anywhere in this corpus -- the class card itself (classes.ashcantor.json) ships system.rules: [], and no abilities/ or class-features/ card exists to hold a Passage/Ember mechanic either. Checked pf2e's own generic SpecialResource rule element (pf2e-source/src/module/rules/rule-element/special-resource.ts:24-247) as a possible fit: every real user (Alchemist's Versatile Vials, Gunslinger's Munitions Machinist, Fumbus's iconic feats) is a daily-refilling consumable counter, never a one-way permanent-increase track like Passage -- no real class resource matches Passage's shape, so there is no base mechanic here to extend or modify. Specifically, this modifies "a Passing"'s targeting requirements and its Passage-threshold cost, both entirely unmodeled.
